The Last Flame

She reaches the far shore still holding one unlit flame. The shore-keeper offers her the river's water; she shakes her head: "I'm keeping it, until she comes." She sits on the stone steps of the far shore, and whenever someone crosses, she holds the flame a little higher.
Home
She opens her hand, and the flames she had left fall one by one into the river, like a string of tiny stars. The far shore has no doorstep and no snow. She never has to sell anything again.
Somewhere Warm
She drinks the river's water. The cold leaves first, then the hunger, then the name of that street. In the end she remembers only this: there was somewhere very warm, and at last she has reached it.
Everything in the Flames
The stove, the roast goose, the Christmas tree, Grandmother: she tells the shore-keeper about each of them, and by the end she has forgotten the beginning. The shore-keeper does not hurry her.
